messages:
elaine: FYI — competitor rolled out a per-tenant fast-fallback routing feature this morning. Getting a few customer questions already. Do we want to go parity or lean into our own angle? :thinking:

sam: Seen it. Their approach is basically routing to cheaper small models when load spikes. Low lift shim for them but loses quality on edge cases.

anya: Can we quantify how often fallback actually impacts end-user quality for our customers? I can run an eval on 3 tenant workloads if we decide to spike.

divya: Sales: multiple pilots asked about 'predictable fallback to cheaper model' because of cost spikes. If we can't offer something similar, competitive RFQs will mention it.

mike: Quick thought: offer a configurable fallback policy (latency-first, cost-first, quality-preserve). That keeps parity but lets us differentiate on policy granularity.

tara: Research: we have telemetry showing 8% of requests in a particular burst profile would be candidates for safe fallback (prefix cached, short context). We should simulate user-facing quality regression curves before committing.

elaine: Proposal: 1) run a 1-week spike (anya + tara) to measure quality delta for two fallback modes; 2) spike eng effort to prototype a policy toggle in routing layer (sam + mike) limited to Dedicated customers; 3) define launch criteria. Thoughts?

sam: OK. For prototype we can do routing flag `route.fallback_policy` with values `latency`, `cost`, `quality`. Implementation plan: route decision in admission path, then select model variant. Low-risk canary behind feature flag. Est 2 devs x 2 sprints to a minimal prototype.

anya: I'll need 3 prompt sets per customer type (chat assistant, doc-summarize, extraction). ETA: 5 working days to produce evals and baseline.

divya: If we gate initial rollout to Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private, that buys us time on capacity and gives customers an enterprise reason to commit. Sales can market it as "policy-backed fallback controls".

mike: Agree. Also need console UX: per-tenant toggle, default policy + override via API. Low priority mock: a single select + tooltip. I can do a quick figma in 48 hours.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: deploy queued — canary cluster upgrade scheduled at 2024-06-07T03:00Z.

elaine: Draft launch criteria (v0):
- Quality regression on evaluation < 3% weighted by customer importance
- End-to-end p95 latency improvement > 15% in cost-first mode for target bursts
- Console and API controls in place for tenant-level toggle
- Canary rollout path + rollback within 15 minutes
- Docs + sales one-pager ready

tara: Add: telemetry alert for quality drift (rolling 30m) and an automated rollback on >5% regression for top 3 tenants.

sam: Risk note: implementing multiple model variants increases cache complexity (KV cache priming and invalidation). Budget ~ +10% engineering ops for rollout.

elaine: Prioritization ask: Where does this sit against the Q3 items? I'm proposing a short cross-functional spike this sprint, then a decision gate at next PRD sync.

divya: Sales: if we can commit to Dedicated-only beta within 6 weeks, I can book three pilot meetings. That buys us credibility.

anya: I'll start evals today and post results in this thread by EOD Friday.

sam: I'll carve out one engineer to pair with mike for the prototype scaffold next sprint. We'll target a canary endpoint and a feature-flagged rollout.

mike: I'll drop the figma and a mini-API spec here in 48 hours: sample API: `POST /v1/fallbacks` body: `{ "tenant_id": "t_123", "policy": "cost" }`. Keep it minimal.

elaine: Solid. Outcome we want at PRD sync: metric-backed recommendation (parity shim vs design-led policy), dev estimate, and go/no-go for Dedicated beta. If all aligns, roadmap add = small cross-team slice (2 sprints engineering + 1 sprint UX + evals).

divya: :thumbsup: I'll prep pilot list.

ops-bot: Reminder: PRD sync scheduled 2024-06-10 16:00 UTC.

elaine: Thanks everyone — if you add anything to the scope or constraints, post here. Otherwise I'll synthesize into a short PRD and link it to the sync. :rocket:
